result.reason: The new cap, listed carve-outs, payment-obligation treatment, and general consequential-damages exclusion largely track the preferred position. However, the retained sentence stating that “under no circumstance” Licensor is liable for claims alleging infringement or violation of IP rights creates an absolute, unilateral exclusion that conflicts with the uncapped IP-infringement carve-out and defeats mutuality. The fee lookback also runs from the event giving rise to the claim rather than the claim itself. In addition, applying all Excluded Claims as exceptions to the consequential-damages waiver goes beyond a playbook requiring those claims only to be uncapped. Drafting quality is impaired by the contradictory provisions, run-on structure, typo (“LICENSORHAS”), and remaining Licensor-specific language.
